 1          Plaintiff Jacqueline Uceta (“Plaintiff”) brings this Class Action Complaint on behalf of
 2   herself, and all others similarly situated, against Defendant Discord, Inc. (“Defendant” or

 5   knowledge:
 6                                         NATURE OF THE CASE
 7          1.         Plaintiff brings this class action against Defendant Discord, Inc. for its failure to
 8   properly secure and safeguard Plaintiff’s and other similarly situated individuals (“Class
 9   Members”) personally identifying information, including names, government-ID images (e.g.,
10   driver’s license, passport), Discord usernames, emails and other contact details if provided to
11   Discord customer support, limited billing information such as payment type, the last four digits of
12   credit card numbers, and purchase history if associated with Discord account, IP addresses, and
13   messages with Discord’s customer service agents (collectively “PII” or “Private Information”). 1
14          2.         Discord, Inc. is a technology company that operates an online communication
15   platform enabling users to connect through voice, video, and text chat across communities and
16   private groups.
17          3.         Plaintiff and Class Members are individuals who were required to indirectly and/or
18   directly provide Defendant with their Private Information. By collecting and storing Plaintiff’s and
19   Class Members’ Private Information, Discord has a resulting duty to secure, maintain, protect, and
20   safeguard the Private Information that it collects against unauthorized access and disclosure
21   through reasonable and adequate data security measures.
22          4.         Despite Discord’s duty to safeguard the Private Information of Plaintiff and Class
23   Members, their Private Information was compromised when an unauthorized party gained access

 1   to Defendant’s third-party customer support services and exfiltrated sensitive data stored therein

 5          6.      While Defendant claims to have discovered the breach as early as September 20,
 6   2025, Defendant did not inform victims of the Data Breach until October 3, 2025. Indeed, Plaintiff
 7   and Class Members were wholly unaware of the Data Breach for nearly a month until they received
 8   letters from Defendant informing them of it.
 9          7.      Indeed, it was not until October 3, 2025 when Plaintiff received an email from
10   Defendant notifying her of the Data Breach and theft of her PII.
11          8.      Discord maintained the PII of Plaintiff and Class Members in a negligent and/or
12   reckless manner. In particular, Defendant should have been aware of the risks of third-party
13   vulnerabilities and weak access controls. The PII was maintained on a computer system and
14   network in a condition vulnerable to cyberattacks. Upon information and belief, the mechanism of
15   the cyberattack and potential for improper disclosure of Plaintiff’s and Class Members’ PII was a
16   known risk to Defendant, and thus Defendant was on notice that failing to take steps necessary to
17   secure the PII from those risks left that property in a dangerous condition.
18          9.      Defendant disregarded the rights of Plaintiff and Class Members by intentionally,
19   willfully, recklessly, and/or negligently failing to implement adequate and reasonable measures to
20   ensure that Plaintiff’s and Class Members’ PII was safeguarded, failing to take available steps to
21   prevent unauthorized disclosure of data and failing to follow applicable, required and appropriate
22   protocols, policies, and procedures regarding the encryption of data, even for internal use.

 5   basic security procedures, Plaintiff’s and Class Members’ Private Information is now in the hands
 6   of cybercriminals.
 7          12.     Plaintiff and Class Members are now at a significantly increased and certainly
 8   impending risk of fraud, identity theft, intrusion of their, and similar forms of criminal mischief,
 9   risk which may last for the rest of their lives. Consequently, Plaintiff and Class Members must
10   devote substantially more time, money, and energy to protect themselves, to the extent possible,
11   from these crimes.
12          13.     Plaintiff, on behalf of herself and all others similarly situated, alleges claims for
13   negligence, breach of implied contract, unjust enrichment and declaratory judgment arising from
14   the Data Breach. Plaintiff seeks damages and injunctive relief, including the adoption reasonably
15   sufficient practices to safeguard the Private Information in Defendant’s custody to prevent
16   incidents like the Data Breach from reoccurring in the future, and for Defendant to provide identity
17   theft protective services to Plaintiff and Class Members for their lifetimes.
18                                                PARTIES
19          14.     Plaintiff Jacqueline Uceta is an adult, who at all relevant times, was a resident and
20   citizen of the State of Florida. Plaintiff received a data breach notice informing her that her Private
21   Information indirectly and/or directly provided to Discord was compromised during the Data
22   Breach.
23          15.     Plaintiff has suffered actual injury from having her Private Information exposed
24   and/or stolen as a result of the Data Breach, including: (a) required mitigation efforts, including
25   researching the Data Breach and needing to monitor her financial statements to ensure her
26   information is not used for identity theft and fraud; (b) damages to and diminution of the value of
27   her Private Information, a form of intangible property that loses value when it falls into the hands

 1   of criminals; (c) loss of privacy; and (d) continuous imminent and impending injury raising from

14          19.     This Court has personal jurisdiction over Defendant because a substantial part of
15   the events, omissions, and acts giving rise to the claims herein occurred in this District and
16   Defendant resides in this District.
17          20.     Pursuant to 28 U.S.C. § 1391, this Court is the proper venue for this action because

21          21.     Defendant is a technology company that develops and operates a digital
22   communication platform designed to enable individuals and communities to connect through
23   voice, video, and text chat, offering tools for social interaction, collaboration, and online
24   community management across a wide range of interests and industries.

 1          22.     Plaintiff and Class Members are and/or were customers of Defendant.

 3   directly or indirectly entrusted Discord with their sensitive Private Information.
 4          24.     Plaintiff and Class Members value the confidentiality of their Private Information
 5   and, accordingly, have taken reasonable steps to maintain the confidentiality of their Private
 6   Information.
 7          25.     In entrusting their Private Information to Defendant, Plaintiff and Class Members
 8   reasonably expected that Defendant would safeguard their highly sensitive information.
 9          26.     By obtaining, collecting, and storing Plaintiff’s and Class Members’ Private
10   Information, Discord assumed equitable and legal duties to safeguard Plaintiff’s and Class
11   Members’ highly sensitive information, to only use this information for business purposes, and to
12   only make authorized disclosures.
13          27.     Despite these duties, Discord failed to implement reasonable data security measures
14   to protect Plaintiff’s and Class Members’ Private Information and ultimately allowed threat actors
15   to exfiltrate Plaintiff’s and Class Members’ Private Information.
16   THE VALUE OF PRIVATE INFORMATION AND EFFECTS OF UNAUTHORIZED DISCLOSURE
17          28.     Discord understood that the Private Information it collects was highly sensitive and
18   of significant value to those who would use it for wrongful purposes.
19          29.     Discord also knew that a breach and exposure of the Private Information, would
20   result in the increased risk of identity theft and fraud against the individuals whose Private
21   Information was compromised.
22          30.     These risks are not theoretical; in recent years, numerous high-profile breaches
23   have occurred at business such as Equifax, Facebook, Yahoo, Marriott, Anthem, and many others.
24          31.     Moreover, Defendant itself was previously a victim of a breach back in March,
25   2023 wherein almost 200 individuals had their information stolen. 5

 1          32.     Private Information has considerable value and constitutes an enticing and well-
 2   known target to hackers. Hackers can easily sell stolen data as there has been “proliferation of
 3   open and anonymous cybercrime forums on the Dark Web that serve as a bustling marketplace for

 6   of crimes including identity theft, and medical and financial fraud. 7 The prevalence of data

 1          35.     In tandem with the increase in data breaches, the rate of identity theft complaints
 2   has also increased over the past few years. For instance, 2024 had the second-highest number of
 3   data compromises in the U.S. in a single year since such instances began being tracked in 2005. 11
 4          36.     The ramifications of Discord’s failure to keep Plaintiff’s and Class Members’
 5   Private Information secure are long-lasting and severe. Once Private Information is stolen,
 6   fraudulent use of that information and damage to victims may continue for years. According to the
 7   U.S. Government Accountability Office, which conducted a study regarding data breaches: “[I]n
 8   some cases, stolen data may be held for up to a year or more before being used to commit identity
 9   theft. Further, once stolen data have been sold or posted on the [Dark] Web, fraudulent use of that
10   information may continue for years. As a result, studies that attempt to measure the harm resulting
11   from data breaches cannot necessarily rule out all future harm.” 12
12          37.     Even if stolen Private Information does not include financial or payment card
13   account information, that does not mean there has been no harm, or that the breach does not cause
14   a substantial risk of identity theft. Freshly stolen information can be used with success against
15   victims in specifically targeted efforts to commit identity theft known as social engineering or
16   spear phishing. In these forms of attack, the criminal uses the previously obtained PII about the
17   individual, such as name, address, email address, and affiliations, to gain trust and increase the
18   likelihood that a victim will be deceived into providing the criminal with additional information.
19          38.     The specific types of personal data compromised in the Data Breach makes the
20   information particularly valuable to thieves and leaves Plaintiff and other Class Members
21   especially vulnerable to identity theft, tax fraud, credit and bank fraud, and more.
22          39.     Passport Numbers—As explained by Aura, a leading identity theft protection
23   service, “[p]assports are among the most widely accepted forms of identification, making them
24   prime targets for scammers and fraudsters. If scammers steal your passport number, they can

14   INFORMATION

15           42.     On or about September 20, 2025, Discord became aware of a cybersecurity event

16   impacting its third-party customer service provider. Following the discovery of the incident,

17   Defendant began an investigation to discover the scope of the suspicious activity.

18           43.     Defendant’s investigation confirmed that on or about September 20, 2025, an

19   unauthorized third-party had gained access to Defendant’s third-party customer support services

20   and successfully exfiltrated Private Information stored therein. The Private Information exfiltrated

21   in the Data Breach includes individuals, names, government-ID images (e.g., driver’s license,

22   passport), Discord usernames, emails and other contact details if provided to Discord customer

23   support, limited billing information such as payment type, the last four digits of credit card

 5   Information of certain of its customers. According to the platform’s data, Discord is used by over

14             47.       Based on Defendant’s announcement of the Data Breach the cyberattack was
15   expressly designed to gain access to private and confidential data of specific individuals, including

19             48.       The Data Breach occurred as a direct result of Discord’s failure to implement and
20   follow basic security procedures to protect its current and former customers’ Private Information
21   that it had collected and stored.

24   Act”) from engaging in “unfair or deceptive acts or practices in or affecting commerce.” The
25   Federal Trade Commission (“FTC”) has concluded that a company’s failure to maintain reasonable

 4           56.     Discord admits that an unauthorized third-party accessed its information
 5   technology system and that Defendant discovered this unauthorized access on or about September
 6   20, 2025. 20
 7           57.     Discord failed to take necessary precautions and failed to employ adequate
 8   measures necessary to protect its computer systems against unauthorized access and keep
 9   Plaintiff’s and Class Members’ Private Information secure.
10           58.     The Private Information that Discord allowed to be exposed in the Data Breach is
11   the type of private information that Discord knew or should have known would be the target of
12   cyberattacks.
13           59.     Despite its own knowledge of the inherent risks of cyberattacks, and
14   notwithstanding the FTC's data security principles and practices, 21 Discord failed to disclose that
15   its systems and security practices were inadequate to reasonably safeguard individuals’ Private
16   Information.
17           60.     The FTC directs businesses to use an intrusion detection system to expose a breach
18   as soon as it occurs, monitor activity for attempted hacks, and have an immediate response plan if
19   a breach occurs. 22 Immediate notification to individuals impacted by a data breach is critical so
20   that those impacted can take measures to protect themselves.
21           61.     Here, Discord inexcusably waited for nearly one month after the Data Breach
22   occurred to notify impacted individuals.
